title: Reduce SLO-pager noise by stratified thresholds and transient suppression
creator: Marisol Cheng
description: After the 2026-01-28 dedicated-capacity regression, we observed a high volume of SLO breach pages generated by short-window burn alerts and transient error spikes. Pager fatigue reduced on-call responsiveness and obscured genuine capacity regressions. This ticket defines follow-up actions to reduce noise while preserving rapid detection of meaningful SLO breaches across Hosted and Dedicated tiers.
acceptance_criteria: Pager volume attributable to transient spikes reduced by >= 60% for noncritical routes during simulated spike runs
Burn-window-based paging replaced with stratified rolling-window thresholds per service tier and capacity-utilization buckets
Runbook updated and validated: clear escalation matrix and post-page triage checklist
Automated test harness for transient suppression added to CI that can reproduce detected-noise pattern
Dashboards show expected vs actual paging rate changes for two weeks post-rollout
actions: A1: Implement stratified paging thresholds - define latency/error thresholds per customer tier (hosted/dedicated/private) and per-capacity-utilization bucket. Owner: Omar Patel. ETA: 2026-03-15.
A2: Replace fixed short burn-window alerts with dual-window evaluation: 60s rapid detector + 15m confirmation window before paging for noncritical routes. Owner: Systems Reliability. ETA: 2026-03-12.
A3: Add transient-suppression heuristic that uses rolling-median smoothing and minimum-volume guardrails to avoid paging on single-burst anomalies. Owner: Infra-SIG (Walter Lin). ETA: 2026-03-18.

A4: Tag routes with customer-impact metadata and route critical customers to aggressive paging; noncritical to silent-ops and async incident emails. Owner: Product Reliability (Anya Ruiz). ETA: 2026-03-20.
A5: Create CI load-scenario for the 2026-01-28 regression pattern; validate new thresholds reduce false pages in regression replay. Owner: ENG-qa (J. Lee). ETA: 2026-03-11.
A6: Update Console runbooks and on-call playbooks, include decision matrix and example traces/alerts. Owner: DevEx (Marisol Cheng). ETA: 2026-03-14.
A7: Post-deploy monitoring: 14-day observation window, with daily digest to SRE & Pager rotation leads. Owner: Observability (Priya Desai). ETA: 2026-03-27.

notes: Decision log: prefer behavioral suppression + stratified thresholds over bluntly increasing burn-rate thresholds because it preserves fast detection for high-volume critical routes.
Trade-offs: small increase in mean detection latency for low-impact routes (median +25-40s) acceptable to reduce cognitive load on on-call teams.
Fallback plan: if suppression causes missed real regressions during observation window, revert to previous alerts and iterate on heuristics.
